newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap-July gas oil done on prompt sell.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap-July gas oil done on prompt sell.

text.p: Singapore front month gas oil swaps weakened at midday on Thursday due to worries that a prompt physical overhang could lead to a new round of price cuts, traders said.
"July gas oil is looking weak because of the physical overhang and people are worried that prices could take another big cut," a trader said.
July swaps were indicated at $22.20/$22.30 per barrel, down 20 cents from Wednesday while August was quoted unchanged at $22.85/$22.95, brokers said.
August traded earlier in the day at $22.90, they said.
Traders said there were fears that more unsold physical barrels will be offloaded in the local spot market as the market moves forward to trade second half July barrels.
On Wednesday, a European major sold to a Chinese trader 30,000 tonne for July 17-21 lifting at $163 per tonne or around $21.90 per barrel free-on-board (fob) Singapore basis.
Traders said more barrels could emerge as sellers have been holding back in expectation of fresh demand from China which has yet to buy in a big way.
"Some people are getting desperate and they may come out to sell aggressively on a fixed price basis," a trader said.
Signs of their need to sell barrels quickly were seen earlier when deals were done at about 60 cents and 75 cents below spot Singapore quotes on a fob basis.
The jet fuel swaps were steady as the market adjusted to the lower level in the face of increased supplies from local refiners and arbitrage cargoes.
July regrade was last quoted steady at $1.80/$2.00 per barrel.
Fuel oil is also unchanged with July swaps quoted at $98.25/$99.50 per tonne.

Naphtha swaps firmed because of the recent crude rally and possible production cut in Japan due to the oil spill in Tokyo Bay. August swaps were last quoted at $20.90/$21.10, up from Wednesday's $20.70/$20.90, brokers said.
August traded late on Wednesday at $20.90, $20.95. $20.80, and $20.85, they said.
